266: Bakr ibn 'Abdullah, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "The Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to throw melons at each other in fun, but when it came to seriousness, they were real men."
261: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with them both, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "The spirits of believers meet at a distance of a day's journey even though they have not seen each other."
262: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Blessings are shown ingratitude and ties of kinship are severed, and I have not seen anything more resembling the hearts of men than intimate friendship."
265: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "O Messenger of Allah, you joke with us!" He said, "Indeed, though I joke with you, I only speak the truth."
263: Umayr ibn Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "We used to say that the first thing to be removed from people is harmony and love."
264: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered upon one of his wives while Umm Sulaym, may Allah be pleased with her, was among them, and he said, "Gently, Unaysa, with the glass vessels!" Abu Qilaba said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, only commanded them regarding this in case there was among them one who might say something unbecoming, and what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, meant was, 'Gently with the pitchers!'"
260: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "By the One in whose hand my soul is, you will not enter the Garden until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I tell you of something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among yourselves. Beware of rancour and enmity, for it is the shaver - I do not mean the shaver of hair, but the shaver of the deen." It was also related in a similar way by another route from Ibrahim ibn Usayd.
267: Ibn Abi Mulayka said that A’isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said a joking word in the presence of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Her mother said, "O Messenger of Allah, some people among the Banu Kinana have brought this kind of joking speech." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Rather, it is we who speak from their language."
269: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to mix with us, so much so that he would say to a younger brother of mine, 'Abu 'Umayr, what has happened to the nughayr?'"
270: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took the hand of al-Hasan or al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them, and placed his feet on his own blessed foot. Then he said, 'Climb up.'"
268: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said that a man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asking him for a mount. He said, "I will give you the young of a she-camel to ride." The man said, "Messenger of Allah, what would I do with the young of a she-camel?" He said, "Is there anything that gives birth to camels except she-camels?"
271: Abu'd-Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "There is nothing heavier in the balance than good character."
272: Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was never coarse nor did he behave coarsely, and he used to say, 'The best of you are those with the best character.'"
273: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with them, said that he heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, "Shall I not tell you which of you is most beloved to me and closest to me in sitting on the Day of Rising?" The people remained silent, so he repeated his words two or three times. The people said, "Yes, Messenger of Allah!" He said, "Those of you with the best character."
274: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "I have only been sent to perfect good character."
278: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I served the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for ten years, and he never once said 'Uff' to me, nor did he ever say regarding something I had not done, 'Why did you not do it?' nor did he say regarding something I had done, 'Why did you do it?'"
280: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was never asked for anything and said, 'No.'"
276: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Allah, the Exalted, has apportioned your characters among you just as He has apportioned your provision among you. Allah, the Exalted, gives wealth to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He only gives faith to whomever He loves. Whoever is miserly in spending, fearful of fighting the enemy, and does not find within himself the resolve to stand in prayer at night, let him say frequently: 'There is no god but Allah,' 'Glory be to Allah,' 'Praise be to Allah,' and 'Allah is greater.'"
279: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was the most merciful and compassionate of people. No one who asked him for something came to him without him promising it, and if he had something with him, he would give it. One day while the prayer was being called, a Bedouin came to him and took hold of his cloak and said, "There is a small matter remaining which I am afraid I will forget, so listen to me." He stood with him until he had finished speaking, and then he came and prayed.
282: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Dust in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell will never gather together inside a slave, and miserliness and faith will never gather together in the heart of a slave."
277: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Richness is not having many possessions. Rather, true richness is the richness of the soul."
281: Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them, said, "I never saw two women more generous than 'A'isha and Asma', may Allah be pleased with them, though their generosity took different forms. 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, used to gather things until she had accumulated something and then she would spend it, while Asma', may Allah be pleased with her, did not save anything for the morrow. Whatever came to her, she would spend it."
275: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was never given the choice between two matters but he chose the easier of the two, as long as it was not a sin. If it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never took revenge for himself in any matter, but if one of the things which Allah had made inviolable was violated, he would become angry for the sake of Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic."
283: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Two qualities do not combine in a believer: miserliness and bad character."
285: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "A man reaches, by his good character, the rank of one who stands in prayer at night."
287: Thabit ibn 'Ubayd, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "I never saw a man more dignified in the gatherings of his companions and more given to joking in his house than Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him."
286: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I heard Abu'l-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, 'The best of you in Islam are those with the best character, when they have understanding of the religion.'"
288: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked, "Which religion is most beloved to Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic?" He said, "The tolerant Hanifiyya."
289: Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said, "If you are given four things, whatever you miss of this world will not harm you: good character, eating what is lawful, truthfulness in speech, and safeguarding trusts."
284: Abdullah ibn Rabi'a, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "We were with Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and he mentioned a man, referring to his character. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, 'What do you think - if you cut off his head, would you be able to put it back?' They said, 'No.' He said, 'What about his hand?' They said, 'No.' He said, 'What about his foot?' They said, 'No.' Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said, 'Since you are not able to change his form, you are not able to change his character. The drop of semen remains in the womb for forty nights, and then it becomes a clot, and then it becomes a lump of flesh. Then Allah, the Exalted, sends an angel who writes down his provision, his character, and whether he is doomed or blessed.'"
290: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Do you know what most commonly causes people to enter the Fire?" They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said, "The private parts and the mouth. And what most commonly causes people to enter the Garden is fear of Allah and good character."
291: Umm al-Darda, may Allah be pleased with her, said, "Abu'l-Darda, may Allah be pleased with him, got up to pray at night and began to weep, saying, 'O Allah, You have made my creation good, so make my character good.' He continued to say this until morning came. I said, 'Abu'l-Darda, you have not stopped supplicating for good character until morning came!' He said, 'Umm al-Darda, when a Muslim slave has good character, that brings him into the Garden, and when he has bad character, that brings him into the Fire. And when a Muslim slave sleeps, he is forgiven.' I said, 'Abu'l-Darda, how is the one who is sleeping forgiven?' He said, 'His brother gets up in the night and prays tahajjud, and then he supplicates Allah, Almighty and Exalted, and his supplication is answered. Then he supplicates for his brother, and his supplication is answered for his brother.'"
295: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked, 'What is it that most causes people to enter the Garden?' He said, 'Fear of Allah and good character.'" He said, "Then he was asked, 'What is it that most causes people to enter the Fire?' He said, 'The mouth and the private parts.'"
293: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was the most generous of people, and he was at his most generous during Ramadan when Jibril the Trustworthy would meet him. Jibril, peace be upon him, would meet him every night during Ramadan and go through the Qur'an with him. When Jibril met him, he was more generous with good than the wind that is sent forth."
294: Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "A man from among those who came before you was brought to account, and no good was found for him except that he used to mix with people, and he was well-off, and he would order his servants and young men to overlook the debt of one in straitened circumstances. Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, said, 'We are more entitled to that than he was,' so He overlooked his debt."
292: Usama ibn Sharik, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, during the Hajj, and the bedouin came, some from here and some from there. The people fell silent and no one spoke except them. They said, 'Messenger of Allah, is there any harm in such and such?' and they mentioned things in which there was no harm. He said, 'Allah has removed hardship and constraint, except for a man who devours his brother's flesh unjustly. It is he who is in hardship and ruin.' They said, 'Messenger of Allah, should we seek medical treatment?' He said, 'Seek medical treatment, slaves of Allah, for Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, has not sent down any disease without sending down a cure for it, except for one disease.' They said, 'Messenger of Allah, what is that?' He said, 'Old age.' They said, 'Messenger of Allah, what is the best and finest thing a man can be given?' He said, 'Good character.'"
296: an-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about righteousness and sin, and he said, 'Righteousness is good character, and sin is what wavers in your soul and which you dislike people finding out about.'"
298: Warrad, the scribe of al-Mughira, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Mu'awiya, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, may Allah be pleased with him, saying, 'Write to me a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.' Al-Mughira wrote back, 'The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to forbid idle talk and rumour-mongering, wasting wealth, excessive asking, reminding people of favours done to them, being undutiful to mothers, and burying daughters alive.'"
297: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "O Banu Salima, who is your chief?" We said, "Judayy ibn Qays, though we consider him miserly." He said, "What sickness is more severe than miserliness? Rather, your chief is 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh." 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh had been the custodian of their idols during the Days of Ignorance. Then, whenever the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, married, he would take charge of his wedding feast.
299: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was never asked for anything and said, 'No.'"
301: Ubaydullah ibn Mihsan al-Ansari reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Whoever among you wakes up secure in his community, healthy in his body, and having his sustenance for the day, it is as if the whole world had been gathered for him."
303: An-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about righteousness and sin. He said, 'Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which wavers in your breast and which you dislike people finding out about.'"
300: Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered me to come to him wearing my battle clothes and my weapon, so I did that. When I came to him, he was doing wudu. He raised his eyes to me and then lowered his head. Then he said, 'Amr, I want to send you out in command of an army, and Allah will grant you booty, and I desire good wealth for you.' I said, 'I did not become Muslim for the sake of wealth. Rather, I became Muslim out of desire for Islam and to be with the Messenger of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'Amr, good wealth is excellent for a good man.'"
302: Ubayda ibn Abdu'l-Hayy reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came with the traces of ghusl on him and his face was cheerful, so they thought that he had just been in private with his wife. They said, "Messenger of Allah, we see that your face is cheerful today." He said, "Praise be to Allah, that is how it is." Then wealth and abundance were mentioned, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "There is nothing wrong with wealth for one who has taqwa, and good health for one who has taqwa is better than wealth, and cheerfulness of the self is one of the blessings of Allah."
305: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Every good deed is sadaqa, and it is part of doing good that you meet your brother with a cheerful face, and that you pour what is left in your bucket into the vessel of your brother."
304: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was the most handsome of people in face, the most generous of people in hand, and the bravest of people. One night the people of Madina were alarmed, so the people went out towards the sound. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, met them, having already gone ahead of the people to the sound by himself, saying, 'You have not been frightened, do not be alarmed.' He was on a horse belonging to Abu Talha, without a saddle, with his sword around his neck. Then he said, 'I found this horse to be like the sea,' or he said, 'It is indeed like the sea.'"
306: Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, said that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked, "Which action is best?" He said, "Belief in Allah and jihad in His way." He asked, "Which slave is best (to free)?" He said, "The one who costs the most and is most valued by his people." He asked, "What if I cannot do that?" He said, "Then help a craftsman or make something for someone unskilled." He asked, "What if I cannot do that?" He said, "Then refrain from doing evil to people, for that is a sadaqa which you give yourself."
308: Abdullah bin Amr bin al-As, may Allah be pleased with them both, said that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say frequently, "O Allah, I ask You for well-being, chastity, trustworthiness, good character, and contentment with the decree."
307: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Every Muslim must give sadaqa." They asked, "What if he does not find anything to give?" He said, "Then let him work with his hands, benefiting himself, and give sadaqa." They asked, "What if he is not able to do that or does not do it?" He said, "Then let him help someone in need who is suffering." They asked, "What if he is not able to do that or does not do it?" He said, "Then let him enjoin what is good." They asked, "What if he is not able to do that or does not do it?" He said, "Then let him refrain from evil, for that is a sadaqa on his part."
476: Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Allah, the Exalted, is Gentle and loves gentleness. He gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness."
477: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Make things easy and do not make them difficult, and give glad tidings and do not repel people."
348: Umm al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with her, said, "Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, came to us from al-Mada'in on foot, wearing a waist-wrap and trousers, the lower part of which he had raised." Ibn Shawdhab said, "Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, was seen wearing a waist-wrap, with his head shaved and his ears large and drooping. It was said to him, 'You have changed your appearance!' He said, 'The real good is the good of the Next World.'"
479: Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, said, "I was on a difficult camel and started to hit it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'Be gentle, for gentleness does not enter into anything except that it adorns it, and it is not removed from anything except that it disgraces it.'"
475: Kathir ibn 'Ubayd, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "I visited the Mother of the Believers, 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and she said, 'Wait until I mend my cloak.'" Kathir said, "So I waited, and then I said, 'Mother of the Believers, if I went out and told people that you patch up an old garment, they would count it as a sign of your miserliness.'" She said, "Understand what is said. The matter is simply that whoever has not worn the old garment has no right to a new one."
478: Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said, "Among the Banu Isra'il there was a man who was staying as a guest, and there was a cat in the house. He said to it, 'O cat, do not hiss at our guest.' Then its young ones, which were still in her belly, began to hiss. This was mentioned to his Prophet, peace be upon him, and he said, 'Its likeness is the likeness of this community which comes after you, in which their ignorant ones will overpower their scholars.'"
482: Al-Harith ibn Laqit, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "There were people among us who, when their mare gave birth to a foal, would slaughter it and say, 'What is the matter with myself that I should ride it?' Then a letter came to us from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, saying, 'Improve what Allah, the Almighty, has provided for you, for the Day of Rising is indeed far off.'"
481: al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Boasting about old age is among the worst of actions."
1205: Abu Hurayra reported that when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, got up in the morning, he would say, "O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is our final return." And when evening came, he would say, "O Allah, by You we enter the evening and by You we enter the morning, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the final destination."
480: Abu Nadra reported that there was a man among his people called Jabir or Juwaybir who related that he came to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, during his caliphate concerning a matter of his own. He arrived in Madina at night, and when morning came, he went to him. He was an intelligent man, eloquent in speech, and he began to censure this world, explaining its evils and putting forward proof that there was no good in it. Beside Umar was a man with a white beard, wearing white garments. When he had finished speaking, the man said, "Everything you have said is correct, except for what you censured regarding this world, for that is not in its proper place. Do you know what this world is? This world is the provision for the Next World, and in it are our actions for which we will be recompensed in the Next World." He said, "A man spoke to me who had more knowledge of this world than I did, so I said, 'Amir al-Mu'minin, who is this beside you?' He said, 'The leader of the Muslims, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him.'"
1206: Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never used to omit this supplication in the evening and in the morning: "O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the Next. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family and my wealth. O Allah, veil my weak points and safeguard me from what I fear. O Allah, protect me from in front of me, from behind me, from my right, from my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being struck down from beneath me."
525:
Aisha said, "When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Madina, Abu Bakr and Bilal fell ill with fever. I went in to see them and said, 'Father, how do you feel? Bilal, how do you feel?'"

She said that when the fever seized Abu Bakr, he would say,

"Every man wakes up among his family, while death is closer than the strap of his sandal."

When it left Bilal, he would raise his voice and say,

"Would that I knew whether I would spend a night in a valley with idhkhir and jalil growing around me! And would I one day go down to the waters of Majanna, and would Shama and Tafil appear before me!"

Aisha said, "I went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and told him about that. He said, 'O Allah, make us love Madina as we love Makka, or even more. Make it healthy and bless our sa` and our mudd for us. Take away its fever and put it in al-Juhfa.'"
1208: Abu Hurayra reported that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication which I can say in the morning and the evening." He said, "Say: 'O Allah, Knower of the Unseen and the Seen, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I testify that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself and from the evil of Shaytan and his shirk.' Say it when you rise in the morning, when you enter upon the evening, and when you lie down to sleep."
1207: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Whoever says when morning comes: 'O Allah, we have entered the morning and the dominion has entered the morning belonging to Allah, and we bear witness to You and to the bearers of Your Throne, and Your angels, and all Your creation, that You are Allah, there is no god but You, alone, without any partner, and that Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is Your slave and Your Messenger' – Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will free a quarter of him from the Fire on that day. Whoever says it twice, Allah will free half of him from the Fire. Whoever says it four times, Allah will free him from the Fire entirely on that day."
1209: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported something similar to the previous hadith, in which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "The Lord of everything and its Sovereign." He also said, "From the evil of Shaytan and his associates."
1211: Hudhayfa, may Allah be pleased with him, said that when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wanted to sleep, he would say, "In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live." And when he woke up from his sleep, he would say, "Praise be to Allah who gave us life after having caused us to die, and to Him is the return."
1212: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said that when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to his bed, he would say, "Praise be to Allah who has fed us, given us drink, sufficed us and given us shelter, for how many are there who have no one to suffice them or give them shelter."
1210: Abu Rashid al-Hibrani said, "I went to 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him, and said, 'Tell me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.' He gave me a written document and said, 'This is a document that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wrote for me.' I looked at it and found in it that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, 'Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication which I can say in the morning and evening.' The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'Abu Bakr, say: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord of everything and its Sovereign, I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself and from the evil of Shaytan and his shirk, and from committing wrong against myself or bringing it upon a Muslim."'"
1214: Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Sleep at the time of remembrance is from Shaytan. Try it if you wish: when one of you goes to his bed and wants to sleep, let him remember Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic."
1213: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not sleep until he had recited Surat as-Sajda and Surat al-Mulk." Abu'z-Zubayr said, "These two suras are superior to every other sura in the Book of Allah by seventy good deeds. Whoever recites them will have seventy good deeds recorded for him, will be raised up seventy levels, and will have seventy bad deeds erased from him."
1217: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I spent the night at the house of my aunt Maymuna. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, got up to pray, so I stood on his left. He took hold of my head and placed me on his right."
1215: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not sleep until he had recited 'Blessed be He in whose Hand is the Kingdom' (Surat al-Mulk) and 'Alif Lam Mim. The revelation of the Book' (Surat as-Sajda)."
1216: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "When any of you lies down on his bed, let him take the inside of his waist-wrap and dust off his bed with it, for he does not know what has come onto it after him. Let him lie down on his right side and say, 'In Your name I have put down my side. O Allah, if You take my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, then protect it in the same way that You protect Your righteous slaves.'"
1218: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, settled into his bed, he would say, "O Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of everything, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, Sender-down of the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an, I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything that has evil, for You hold it by its forelock. You are the First, so there is nothing before You. You are the Last, so there is nothing after You. You are the Outward, so there is nothing above You. You are the Inward, so there is nothing beneath You. Settle my debt for me and free me from poverty."
1219: al-Bara' ibn 'Azib reported that when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, settled into his bed, he would lie on his right side and then say, "O Allah, I submit myself to You, I turn my face to You, I entrust my affair to You, and I lean my back on You, out of desire for You and fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape except to You. I believe in Your Book which You have sent down and in Your Prophet whom You have sent." The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Whoever says these words and then dies that night, dies in a state of fitra."
1221: Al-Bara, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wanted to sleep, he would place his hand under his right cheek and say, "O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the day You raise up Your slaves." It is also related from al-Bara by another route in a similar way.
1224: Rabi'a ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I used to spend the night at the door of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I would hear him say, when he prayed tahajjud, 'Allah hears whoever praises Him,' and I would hear him say, when he finished his prayer, 'Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.'"
1220: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "When a man enters his house or settles onto his bed, an angel and a devil hasten to him. The angel says, 'End with good,' and the devil says, 'End with evil.' If he praises Allah and remembers Him, the angel drives the devil away and guards him throughout his night. Then when he wakes up, the angel and the devil hasten to him and both say the same as before. If he remembers Allah and says, 'Praise be to Allah who has returned my spirit to me after its death and did not let it die in its sleep. Praise be to Allah who holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist, and if they should cease to exist, no one after Him could hold them. He is All-Forbearing, Most Forgiving. Praise be to Allah who holds the sky lest it fall upon the earth except by His permission. He is Ever Compassionate and Merciful to His slaves' - if he then dies, he dies as a martyr, and if he gets up and prays, he prays a prayer of immense merit."
1225: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Whoever sleeps with grease on his hand and does not wash it off, and something happens to him, let him blame no one but himself."
1226: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Whoever sleeps with grease on his hand and something happens to him should only blame himself."
1223: Abu Hurayra reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "When any of you goes to his bed, let him take the edge of his lower garment and shake his bed with it, and let him mention the name of Allah, for he does not know what has come onto his bed after he last used it. Then let him lie down on his right side and say, 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I have restrained myself, I have laid down my side, and You have taken my soul to Yourself. O Allah, if You take my soul, forgive it, and if You keep it, protect it in the way You protect Your righteous slaves.'"
1222: Abdullah bin Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "There is no Muslim who persists in performing two rak'ahs of Duha except that Allah loves them." They asked, "O Messenger of Allah, what are they?" He said, "One of you glorifies Allah at the end of every prayer ten times, praises Him ten times, and magnifies Him ten times. That makes one hundred and fifty on the tongue and one thousand five hundred in the Balance." He - may Allah bless him and grant him peace - began counting them on his hand. He said, "Then he lies down and glorifies Allah thirty-three times, praises Him thirty-three times, and magnifies Him thirty-four times. That makes one hundred on the tongue and one thousand in the Balance. Which of you commits five hundred evil deeds in a day and two nights?" They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how could one not manage this?" He said, "Shaytan comes to one of you during his prayer and reminds him of the needs of this world, so he does not remember to glorify Allah."
1227: Jabir bin Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Close the doors at night, tie up the waterskins, turn over the vessels or cover them, and put out the lamps, for the Shaytan does not open a closed door, undo a tie, or remove a cover, and the mouse can burn down the people's house."
1230: Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Do not leave fire in your houses when you sleep."
1232: Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said that he heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, "Do not leave fire burning in your houses at night, for it is an enemy to you."
1231: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "The Fire is an enemy, so beware of it." Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to check the fire in his house and put it out before he slept.
1228: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "A mouse came and started dragging a wick, and a girl went to stop it, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'Leave it.' It brought the wick and dropped it on the mat which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sitting on, and a dirham-sized part of it was burned. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'When you go to sleep, put out your lamps, for Shaytan guides creatures like this to your negligence so that they burn you.'"
1229: Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, said that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was awake one night and saw a mouse carrying a wick, taking it up to the roof to set fire to the house over them. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cursed it and permitted it to be killed in the Haram.
1233: Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that a house in Madina caught fire at night with its people in it. This was mentioned to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said, "This fire is an enemy of yours, so when you sleep, put it out."
1235: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered that filth be hung up in the house.
1234: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "When the rain fell, he would say, 'Girl, bring out my saddle and my clothes,' and he would recite, 'And We sent down blessed water from the sky.'"
1237: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Call your children back to yourselves until the beginning of the night has passed, for that is the time when the shaytans spread about."
1245: As-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to pass by us close to midday and say, 'Get up and take a nap, for whatever remains of the day belongs to Shaytan.'"
1236: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "When night comes, keep still and do not walk about, for none of you knows what Allah lets loose of His creatures. Close the doors, tie up the water-skins, cover the vessels, and put out the lamps."
1246: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, used to pray Jumu'a and then take a midday nap.
1244: Sa'ib ibn Yazid, may Allah have mercy on him, reported that Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Some men from the Quraysh used to stand at the door of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, to learn something from him. When the shadow shifted, he would say, 'Get up, for whatever remains of the day is for Shaytan,' and then he would pass by them and make them get up firmly." While they were like that, they were told, "This is a young man from Banu Hashish who composes poetry." They called him and said, "What poetry have you composed?" He said, "If you have set out on a journey this morning, then leave Salim alone, for old age and the religion of Islam are sufficient to keep a person from evil." Umar said, "That is enough for you. You have spoken the truth, you have spoken the truth."
1248: Khawwat ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Sleeping at the beginning of the day is ignorance, sleeping in the middle of it is the Sunna, and sleeping at the end of it is stupidity."
1252: Salim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, circumcised me and Nu'aym, and a ram was slaughtered on our behalf. We used to boast about that to the other boys, that a ram had been slaughtered on our behalf."
1251: Umm al-Muhajir reported: "I was brought among the captives of the Byzantines. 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, called us to Islam, and none accepted Islam except myself and one other woman." 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Go and circumcise them and purify them."
1250: Abu Hurayra reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was circumcised when he was eighty years old, and he circumcised himself with an adze." Imam al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Qadum here does not refer to a place, but he means eighty years old."
1249: Maymun ibn Mahran said, "I asked Nafi', 'Did Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, use to invite people to eat?' He said, 'That was not his usual practice, but a camel of his broke its leg, so we slaughtered it. Then he said, "Gather the people of Madina." I said, "Abu 'Abdu'r-Rahman, what should I invite them to? We have no bread." He said, "O Allah, to You belongs all praise. There is meat on the bones and broth" - or he said, "broth and meat" - "Whoever wants can eat and whoever wants can leave it."'"
1253: Umm 'Alqama reported that the daughters of the sisters of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, were circumcised, and it was said to 'A'isha, "Shall we not call someone to entertain them?" She said, "Yes." So someone was sent to 'Adiyy, and he came. 'A'isha passed by him and saw him singing and dancing, with a great deal of hair. 'A'isha said, "Ugh! Take this devil out, take him out."
1254: Aslam, the mawla of 'Umar, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "When we came to Syria with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, a nobleman of the town came to him and said, 'Commander of the Believers, I have prepared some food for you and I would like you to come to my house, along with a group of your prominent companions. That would be a source of strength and honour for me.' 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, 'We do not enter these churches of yours, since they contain those images.'"
1255: Umm Muhajir, may Allah have mercy on her, said, "I and some women slaves were taken captive from the land of the Byzantines. Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, called us to Islam, and I and one other woman became Muslim, but none of the others became Muslim. Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said, 'Circumcise these two and purify them.'" She said, "So I used to serve Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him."
1247:
Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "When the prohibition of wine was revealed, the wine that the people of Madina had was made from unripe dates and dried dates. One day I was serving the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the house of Abu Talha, may Allah be pleased with him, when a man passed by and said, 'Wine has been prohibited.' He did not ask when it had been prohibited nor look into the matter further, but said, 'Anas, pour out this wine.' Then it was mentioned in the house of Umm Sulaym, may Allah be pleased with her, until the heat of the sun had died down, and he bathed. Umm Sulaym then perfumed him, and he went to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and told him what had happened, just as the man had described it."

Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "He never put wine to his lips again after that."
1258: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "When a man became Muslim, he was ordered to be circumcised, even if he was advanced in age."
1257: Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Are you not amazed at Malik ibn al-Mundhir? He went out searching for nine Muslims among the peasants of Byzantium who had recently become Muslim, and he investigated them and ordered that they be circumcised in the winter while the wound was harmful. It has reached me that some of them died. When the Byzantines and the Abyssinians became Muslim during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, nothing about their circumstances was investigated at all."
1256:
Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was circumcised when he was one hundred and twenty years old, and then he lived for another hundred years after that."

Sa'id, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was the first to be circumcised, the first to entertain a guest, the first to clip his moustache and cut his nails, and the first to have grey hair appear. He said, 'My Lord, what is this?' Allah, the Exalted, said, 'This is dignity.' Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said, 'My Lord, increase me in dignity.'"
1283: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, "Someone who plays backgammon is like one who eats the flesh of a pig, and someone who plays it without gambling is like one who dips his hand in the blood of a pig."
1284: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "A believer is not stung twice from the same hole."
1286: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Whoever takes up arms against us is not one of us."
1285:
Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Whoever shoots arrows at us by night is not one of us."

Abu 'Abdullah al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Its chain of transmission is questionable."
1282: Ya'la bin Murra, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "I heard Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, say regarding one who plays chess with gambling stakes, 'He is like one who eats the flesh of a pig.' As for one who plays it without gambling stakes, he is like one who dips his hand in the blood of a pig. And one who sits by it and watches is like one who looks at the flesh of a pig."
1287: Abu Musa al-Ashari, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Whoever takes up arms against us is not one of us."
1288: Abu 'Azza Yasar ibn 'Abd, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "When Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic, wants to take a slave's life in a certain land, He creates a need for him there."
1289: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, wiped his nose with a garment and then said, "Woe to you, woe to you, Abu Hurayra! You wipe your nose with a garment! I have seen myself fall down between the room of A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and the pulpit out of hunger, and a man would pass by and say, 'He is mad,' when there was nothing wrong with me except hunger."
1290: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "O Messenger of Allah, we find within ourselves thoughts which we would consider too great to speak of, even if we were given all that is on the earth." He said, "Do you find that?" They said, "Yes." He said, "That is clear faith."
1292: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "People will continue to ask questions about things that will not happen until they say, 'Allah is the Creator of everything, so who created Allah?'"
1293: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most lying form of speech. Do not spy on one another, do not compete with one another for worldly goods, do not turn away from one another, do not envy one another, and do not hate one another. Be servants of Allah as brothers."
1294: Anas ibn Malik reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was with one of his wives when a man passed by. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called him and said, "O so-and-so, this is my wife, so-and-so." The man said, "I would have thought that of someone other than you, but I would not think that of you." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Shaytan flows in the son of Adam as blood flows."
1291: Shahr ibn Hawshab, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "My uncle and I went to see the Lady A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and we said, 'One of us finds thoughts in his breast which, if he were to voice them, would destroy his hereafter, and if they became known, he would be killed for them.'" She said, "When she heard that, she said, 'Allahu Akbar,' three times and said, 'The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about that and he said, "When something like that comes to one of you, let him say, 'Allahu Akbar' three times, for the believer alone finds something like that."'"
1297: Abdul Aziz ibn Qays, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "I went to Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, while a slave-girl was cutting his hair, and he said, 'Depilatory cream or henna soften the skin.'"
1299: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Five things are part of the fitra: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, and trimming the moustache."
1295: Abdullah ibn Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Whoever has his wealth stolen continues to make accusations until he surpasses the thief in wrongdoing."
1298: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Five things are part of the fitra: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, plucking the armpit hair, trimming the moustache, and cutting the nails."
1300: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Five things are part of the fitra: clipping the nails, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, and circumcision."
1301: Abu Tufayl, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, distributing meat at al-Ji'rana, and I was a boy of nine years old at that time. I was lifting up pieces of camel meat when a woman came to him, and he spread out his cloak for her. I asked, 'Who is this?' It was said, 'This is the woman who suckled you, your mother who nursed you.'"
1296: Bilal ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Mu'awiya, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abu'l-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, telling him to write to him with the names of the profligates of the people of Damascus. Abu'l-Darda' said, 'What have I got to do with the profligates of the people of Damascus? How would I know them?' His son Bilal, may Allah have mercy on him, said, 'I will write their names for you.' So he wrote their names. Abu'l-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, said, 'How did you come to know that about them, and how did you recognise that they were profligates unless you are one of them yourself? Begin with yourself and write down your own name.' So he wrote down the names but did not send them."
1305: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to send my friends to me so that they could play with me with dolls."
1303: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Our companions used to permit us every game except dice." Abu 'Abdullah al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "That is, backgammon."
1302: al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "A man said, 'May Allah set right the amir. Your doorman gives precedence to those he knows when granting admission.' He replied, 'May Allah accept his excuse. Being known is beneficial even in the place of a savage biting dog or a raging camel.'"
1306: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man chasing a pigeon in flight and said, "A devil chasing a she-devil."
1304: Abd al-Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "A righteous shaykh called Abu Uqba told me that he once sat with Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, on a road, and they passed by some Abyssinian boys who were playing. He took out two dirhams and gave them to them."
1307:
Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, used to command in his sermon every Jumua that dogs be killed and pigeons be slaughtered."

In another version from al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, used to command in his sermon that dogs be killed and pigeons be slaughtered.
1309: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "When a man spits in front of people, he should conceal it with his hands until his spittle reaches the ground. When a man is fasting, he should oil his skin so that the effects of fasting do not show on him."
1313: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "There is no good in idle talk."
1308: Zayd ibn Thabit reported: "Umar came to me one day and asked permission to enter, so I gave him permission while my head was in the hand of a slave-girl who was combing it. I wanted to take my head out of the slave-girl's hand, but Umar said, 'Leave her to comb it.' I said, 'Amir al-Mu'minin, if you had sent for me, I would have come to you.' Umar said, 'The matter was my doing, (so it was fitting that I should be the one to come).'"
1310: Habib ibn Abi Thabit, may Allah have mercy on him, liked that when a man spoke, he should not direct his address specifically at one man, but rather make his speech general.
1311: Ibn Abi Hadhil, may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Our master Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, went with one of his companions to visit a sick man. When they entered the house, the people of the house began looking here and there. Our master Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, said to them, 'By Allah, if your eyes had been put out, it would have been better for you.'"
1312: Nafi', may Allah have mercy on him, said, "Some people from Iraq came to our master Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, and he saw a gold necklace around the neck of one of their slave-girls. Some of them began to look at each other, so our master Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said, 'Your eyes are indeed sharp when it comes to seeing evil.'"
1315: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Among the worst of people is the two-faced one, who comes to some people with one face and to others with another face."
1323: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "The strong man is not the one who wrestles well. The strong man is only the one who controls himself when he is angry."
1314: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "The worst and most base of my community are those who talk excessively, who are bombastic in speech, and who twist their mouths affectedly. The best of my community are those with the best character."
1324: Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, "There is no drink which a person drinks that carries a greater reward with Allah than a drink of anger which a person swallows seeking the pleasure of Allah."
1316: Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, 'Whoever has two faces in this world will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Rising.'" Then a large man passed by and he said, "This is one of them."
1326: Sulayman ibn Surad, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I was sitting with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while two men were reviling each other. One of them turned red, and his neck veins swelled up. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'I know a word which, if he said it, his anger would leave him.' The people said to him, 'The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan."' He said, 'Am I mad?'"
1327: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Teach people the religion and make things easy. Teach and make things easy," three times, and he said, "When you become angry, be silent," twice.
1325: Sulayman ibn Surad, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Two men reviled each other in the presence of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of them became so enraged that his face turned red. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'I know a phrase that if he were to say it, his anger would leave him: "I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan (A'udhu billahi min ash-Shaytani'r-rajim)."' A man then got up and went to him and said, 'Do you know what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said?' He said, 'Say: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan.' He replied, 'Do you think I am mad?'"
1329: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "Do not let your love make you act foolishly, and do not let your hatred destroy you." I asked, "How is that?" He said, "When you love, you love like the madness of a child, seeing everything in favour of the one you love, and when you hate, you would like the one you hate to be destroyed."
1328: Ubayd al-Kindi, may Allah have mercy on him, said that he heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, say to Ibn al-Kawwa: "Do you know what the earlier generations used to say? If you love someone, do not go to excess in your love for him, for he might become your enemy one day. And if you hate someone, do not go to excess in your hatred for him, for he might become your friend one day."
